script.base: Roof-closed Lucas Oil, DEN a 2.5-point favorite with implied totals DEN 23.0 and IND 20.5 on a 43.5 total. Base flow is a one-score game into the fourth quarter: Bo Nix leans on J.K. Dobbins (week-1 16 carries, 63 yards) rather than a pass-volume spike, Indianapolis stays balanced with Jonathan Taylor (18 carries, 71 yards) and DJ Giddens (12 carries, 41 yards) because +2.5 is not a 3.5-point abandon-the-run number, and the modest total is run-leaning rather than a shootout.
script.flip1: Denver jumps ahead early, kills the clock with Dobbins, and Nix, Courtland Sutton and Troy Franklin yardage stalls; Indianapolis then throws to Tyler Warren (week-1 9 targets, 76 yards) and Michael Pittman (8 targets, 80 yards) and Taylor's carry count dies.
script.flip2: Indianapolis leads at home, Denver drops the Dobbins lean, and Nix faces Indianapolis's 42% blitz (his week-1 EPA per dropback was -0.30 vs blitz and -0.15 vs no blitz), so checkdowns to Tyler Badie (6 targets) and Evan Engram (4) rise; or the game becomes a defensive slog under 43.5 and every yardage over comes up short.

pre_mortem: It is Monday and the slip lost. Dobbins over lost because Indianapolis's 6.50 yards per carry was one opponent, Harvey again took the long runs (he had 70 on 6 carries in week 1), and Dobbins finished in the high 50s on about 15 carries. Taylor under lost because Greenlaw's absence loosened Denver's fits, Indianapolis controlled the clock at home, and Taylor got 20 carries at a modest yards per carry and walked through 71.5 without a 10-yard run. The other miss is a Denver trail, where the dropped Sutton over against two backup corners would have been the live edge and this line-of-scrimmage stack would have been the wrong story. No price was saved, so even a right read could have been a bad number.
slip_story: One Denver-controls-the-line-of-scrimmage story in a closed roof, not a shootout stack: Dobbins keeps the carry share against the Indianapolis front that allowed 6.50 yards per carry, and Taylor does not repeat 71 rush yards against the Denver front that allowed 3.38 yards per carry and zero runs of 10-plus. Both legs win together if Denver leads and both lose together if Indianapolis controls the clock. Do not add Sutton or Franklin overs, which need a pass script into a 42% blitz, or a Harvey rush over, which needs the explosives Dobbins is supposed to earn. No bet placed.
